title: Design an Internal LLM Platform (Gateway, Routing, Cost)
summary: Many teams, many models, one bill. Design the shared layer every LLM call in a company passes through: a gateway that authenticates, routes, rate-limits, caches, observes and attributes cost per tenant, without becoming the outage that takes everyone down.
objectives: Size an internal LLM platform from request volume: QPS, tokens per day, monthly spend, concurrent streams and log storage
Design a gateway request path and keep its added latency within a budget of tens of milliseconds
Compute the expected cost and quality of routing and cascades, and set per-tenant quotas with token buckets and fair sharing
Decide what to cache, how to key it so tenants never see each other's data, and what it actually saves
Attribute direct and shared costs to tenants, and design for provider and gateway failures
prerequisites: Work through [A Framework for LLM System Design](/learn/llm-system-design/design-framework) first: this case walks the same steps. The deep dives lean on [Choosing and Routing Models](/learn/production-systems/model-routing), [Fallbacks and Graceful Degradation](/learn/production-systems/fallbacks), [Budgets, Rate Limits and Usage Controls](/learn/production-systems/budgets-and-rate-limits), [Observability and Incident Analysis](/learn/production-systems/observability) and [Caching Repeated Work](/learn/inference-and-serving/caching).
